items.title: Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks
items.meta: Sophie Leroy · 2009 · Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
items.what: When you switch tasks, part of your attention stays on the one you left, and the next task suffers for it.

items.title: Executive control of cognitive processes in task switching
items.meta: Joshua Rubinstein, David Meyer, Jeffrey Evans · 2001 · Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
items.what: Every switch between tasks costs time, and the cost grows with the complexity of the tasks.

items.title: The cost of interrupted work: more speed and stress
items.meta: Gloria Mark, Daniela Gudith, Ulrich Klocke · 2008 · CHI
items.what: Interrupted people kept their pace by working faster, and paid for it in stress, frustration and effort.

items.title: Measuring the impact of early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
items.what: Experienced developers working with AI tools took 19% longer on real tasks in their own repositories, while believing they had been about 20% faster.
items.note: 16 developers, 246 tasks, early-2025 tools. Read the authors' caveats before generalising.

items.title: How AI assistance impacts the formation of coding skills
items.what: Developers who handed the code to the AI learned the least; those who kept asking conceptual questions learned the most.

items.title: ParallelPilot: supporting coordination and monitoring in parallel AI coding
items.meta: Tao Long, Weili Shi, Hussein Mozannar, Maya Murad, Rafah Hosn · 2026 · preprint
items.what: For balance: with a tool built for it, people supervising several agents at once closed more short tickets, but did not feel more in control of them.
items.note: 16 participants, short tasks, not yet peer reviewed.

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.what: What happens when coding stops being the bottleneck: source control, review and CI have to be rebuilt, and the engineers' job becomes saying no.

items.title: Build your own AI software factory with Claude Code
items.meta: ZazenCodes · 7 October 2026 · video, sponsored by Anthropic
items.what: A small factory you can run today: a spec writer, a builder, four reviewers and an approver that calls a human when it matters.

items.title: If you thought the speed of writing code was your problem, you have bigger problems
items.what: The pipeline behind the bottleneck section: widen one stage and the queue moves to the next.

items.title: How do software developers spend their time?
items.what: Writing code is about 16% of a developer's time; the rest goes to requirements, security, CI/CD, monitoring, deploying and UX.

items.title: Retort
items.what: Compares tooling stacks across models and environments, baseline against candidate, to decide what to promote or retire.

items.title: promptfoo
items.what: Tests prompts, models and agents against your own cases, so a release can be checked before it ships.
